mark_split.label: List the candidates in the interval

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.108, chapter 9 TRIGONOMETRIC EQUATIONS, Short Answer question 4(i). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 shape gives a WHOLE mark to the final test, because this is the one question in the chapter whose answer is halved by it. EXTRANEOUS-ROOT RECORD: multiplying by cosθ turns tanθ + secθ = √3 into √3 cosθ − sinθ = 1, and that cleared equation is satisfied by θ = 3π/2, where cosθ = 0 and neither tanθ nor secθ exists. It is therefore an extraneous root introduced by the clearing step, and it is discarded on the page with the reason. Only θ = π/6 survives in 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π, and it was substituted into the ORIGINAL equation: 1/√3 + 2/√3 = 3/√3 = √3. A route through squaring (secθ = √3 − tanθ, then sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ) reaches tanθ = 1/√3 and admits θ = 7π/6 instead, which also fails the original — either route needs the same test, and this card takes the shorter one. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Trigonometric Equations supplies one of them. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name each move in order, and say how you would test the values you find.

steps.label: Clear the denominator
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both ratios share the denominator cosθ, so they add straight away. Record cosθ ≠ 0 before multiplying by it — that condition is what the last step uses.
steps.memory_tip: tanθ and secθ share the denominator cosθ, so they add to (sinθ + 1)/cosθ. Record cosθ ≠ 0 first.

recall.must_convey: That tanθ + secθ = (sinθ + 1)/cosθ and multiplying by cosθ gives √3 cosθ − sinθ = 1, with cosθ ≠ 0 recorded.
accept: both terms are over cos theta so it becomes sin theta plus one over cos theta and multiplying gives root three cos theta minus sin theta equals one
note cos theta is not zero then clear the denominator
it turns into the a cos theta plus b sin theta form
rendu terms cos theta meeda unnayi, cos theta tho multiply cheyyali
clear the denominator to get a linear combination

steps.why: tanθ and secθ already sit over the same denominator, so one addition removes the fractions. Writing cosθ ≠ 0 now is what lets you catch the false answer later.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to record cosθ ≠ 0 before multiplying by cosθ.

steps.label: Collapse to one cosine
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Divide by √(a² + b²) = 2 so the coefficients become cos(π/6) and sin(π/6), and the left side becomes one cosine of a compound angle.
steps.memory_tip: Divide by √(a² + b²) = 2, and cos A cos B − sin A sin B = cos(A + B) — the sign is PLUS inside.

recall.must_convey: That dividing by 2 gives cos(θ + π/6) = 1/2 = cos(π/3).
accept: divide by root of a squared plus b squared which is two then the left side is cos of theta plus pi by six
the coefficients become cos pi by six and sin pi by six
it collapses to cos theta plus pi by six equals cos pi by three
two tho divide cheste cos theta plus pi by six vasthundi
use the cos A plus B formula
heard_as: cos theta plus pi by six

steps.why: a cosθ + b sinθ cannot be solved directly, but after dividing by √(a² + b²) the coefficients are always a cosine and a sine of one angle, and a single compound-angle formula finishes it.
common_mistakes: Dividing by a + b instead of √(a² + b²).
Using cos(A − B) and getting θ − π/6.

steps.label: List the candidates in the interval
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Write the cosine general solution, split the ± into two families, then substitute n = 0, 1 and keep whatever lands in 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π. These are candidates, not answers yet.
steps.memory_tip: Split the ± into two separate families before substituting n. Call what you get candidates, not answers.
lines: For cosθ = cosα, θ = 2nπ ± α, so
In 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π, n = 0 gives θ = π/6 and
n = 1 gives θ = 3π/2. These are candidates.

recall.must_convey: That the general solution splits into θ = 2nπ + π/6 and θ = 2nπ − π/2, giving candidates π/6 and 3π/2 inside 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π.
accept: theta plus pi by six is two n pi plus or minus pi by three so theta is two n pi plus pi by six or two n pi minus pi by two
inside zero to two pi the candidates are pi by six and three pi by two
split the plus or minus into two families then substitute n
interval lo pi by six, three pi by two rendu candidates
these are candidates and still have to be tested
heard_as: two n pi plus pi by six
two n pi minus pi by two

steps.why: The ± in the cosine general solution is two different families, and each has to be listed separately before any interval can be applied to it.
common_mistakes: Substituting n into 2nπ ± π/3 and forgetting to subtract π/6.
Writing the second family as 2nπ − π/6 instead of 2nπ − π/2.

steps.label: Test them and reject
steps.margin_note: Last mark, and the point of this question. θ = 3π/2 entered when the equation was multiplied by cosθ; at that value cosθ = 0, so tanθ and secθ do not exist. It is an extraneous root and must be discarded in writing.
steps.memory_tip: Multiplying by cosθ let in the values where cosθ = 0. Test every candidate in the ORIGINAL equation, not the cleared one.
lines: Test both candidates in the original equation.
At θ = 3π/2, cosθ = 0, so tanθ and secθ do
not exist. This value entered only when we
multiplied by cosθ, so it is discarded.

recall.must_convey: That θ = 3π/2 is discarded because cosθ = 0 makes tanθ and secθ undefined, and θ = π/6 is confirmed in the original equation.
accept: at three pi by two cos theta is zero so tan and sec do not exist and it is rejected
it came in when we multiplied by cos theta so it is an extraneous root
put pi by six back and one by root three plus two by root three is root three
three pi by two lo cos theta zero, tan sec undefined, reject
only pi by six passes the test in the original equation

steps.why: Multiplying by cosθ let in the values where cosθ = 0, and at those values the original equation has no meaning at all. Testing every candidate in the ORIGINAL equation is the only way to catch them.
common_mistakes: Writing both θ = π/6 and θ = 3π/2 as answers.
Testing in the cleared equation √3 cosθ − sinθ = 1, which θ = 3π/2 does satisfy.
Giving the general solution when the interval was asked for.
